transcript:
User: I want to be upfront: the last marketing agency strung me along for three months and I got nothing. Why would you be different?
Agent: I hear you—getting dragged for three months with nothing to show for it is brutal. Before I explain how we’re different, what did you hire them to do, specifically, and what result were you expecting?
User: They promised increased bookings. All I got were empty promises and no follow-through. What happens after I sign?
Agent: Got it—“increased bookings” with no follow-through is exactly what you don’t want again. After you sign, Jay sets up the call capture and booking flow end-to-end (so missed calls and after-hours inquiries get answered and booked), then we review the results together early on so you can see what’s actually coming in—what kind of business are you in?
User: I own a dental practice. How do I know I won't get dropped once you have my card?
Agent: I hear you—especially in a dental practice, if you get “set up” and then abandoned, you’re right back to missed calls and lost bookings. When you’ve been “dropped” before, what did that look like day-to-day—were calls going to voicemail, no reporting, no one responding, or something else?
User: Exactly, calls went to voicemail and there was no follow-up or reporting. It was frustrating and costly.
Agent: Yeah—that makes total sense, and it’s costly when dental calls hit voicemail and nobody follows up or shows you what’s happening. Roughly how many calls a week do you think are going to voicemail (including after-hours)?
User: About 18 calls a week, and it's frustrating knowing 60% could book. How can you help prevent this?
Agent: Got it—18 a week is a lot, and if ~60% would’ve booked, that’s real money slipping away.

We prevent it by answering those missed and after-hours calls automatically, capturing the patient details and intent (new patient, hygiene, emergency), and getting them booked or routed correctly—plus you get clear reporting so you can see exactly what happened to every call.

Mind if I do a quick 30‑second calculation on what those 18 missed calls are likely costing you?
User: Go ahead, but I need to see how this actually works before I make any decisions.
Agent: Totally fair—you should see it working before deciding. For the quick math, what’s your average patient value per booked appointment (ballpark: $200, $300, $500)?
User: Average visit is around $240. But I need to see real results before making any commitments.
Agent: Makes sense—you shouldn’t commit on promises.

Using your numbers (18 missed calls/week, ~60% would book, ~$240 average visit), that’s about **$2591 extra a week**—and that’s just one week… about **$11200/mo** over a month. If you started consistently capturing those calls, would you want to see that show up as more new patients booked, more emergencies captured, or both?
User: Both, but I need to see evidence it works before I trust another service.
Agent: Totally fair—I hear you, especially after getting burned.

It’s a 20-minute walkthrough—Jay will show you exactly how it works for a dental office (missed-call capture + emergency routing) and what your numbers look like with it on. What’s better for you—later today or tomorrow?
User: Okay... one demo. But I'm watching closely. Tomorrow works better. Remember, I'm on Mountain/Phoenix time.
Agent: Got it—tomorrow works, and you’re on Mountain (Phoenix) time. What’s your first name?
User: Bianca. Looking forward to the demo. Just want to make sure this is the real deal.
Agent: Absolutely, Bianca—I get wanting proof. What’s your last name?
User: Cole. It's Bianca Cole. Just want to make sure this is a good fit for Cole Family Dental.
Agent: Got it—Bianca Cole at Cole Family Dental. Is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you for the demo confirmation?
User: Yes, the number I called from is best. Just make sure to confirm everything in Mountain/Phoenix time.
Agent: Perfect—I'll keep everything in Mountain (Phoenix) time. For tomorrow, I can get you in as soon as **12:00 PM** or **12:45 PM** Mountain time—which works?
User: 12:00 PM Mountain time works. I'll be ready. Looking forward to seeing how this can help.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Hmm—looks like that 12:00 PM Mountain slot is showing a conflict on the calendar. Do you want to do **12:45 PM Mountain** instead?
User: Sure, take your time. Just need to ensure everything aligns with our Mountain/Phoenix time zone.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Thanks, Bianca! You’re booked for **tomorrow at 12:45 PM Mountain (Phoenix) time**, and you’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details—you can add it to your calendar in one click, or reschedule if you need to.  

Is there anything else I can help you with?
User: Sure, just remember it's Mountain/Phoenix time. I'm looking for real solutions, not just empty promises.
Agent: Absolutely—everything is in Mountain (Phoenix) time, and I hear you on wanting real results, not promises. Really glad you called, Bianca—Jay’s looking forward to it. Have a great rest of your day. Bye!
